newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended firm, with the market seeing little activity apart from continued professional demand for longer-dated cash bonds.
"It was a very quiet day. No real movement, only small customer businesss and slightly better prices. Turnover was concentrated in 2006, 2007 and 2008 bonds," one trader said.
A second trader said the 2007 and 2008 bonds have lately become expensive relative to both swaps and futures.
"In the last two weeks, the bonds have gotten half a point more expensive than futures. Also versus swaps the trend is similar," one trader said.
The Swiss federal June 4-1/2 percent bond yielded 3.66 percent in late trade while 10-year swaps were quoted at a midpoint of around four percent.

Bond traders said there was little reaction to latest statements by Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer. Meyer, speaking at the SNB's annual shareholders' meeting, said that the SNB would have to tighten eventually but it was too early in the recovery to consider such measures now.
An SNB spokesman reconfirmed the central bank was not considering immediate rate changes. He was responding to a reporter's enquiry at the SNB shareholder meeting Friday.

The market was nervous Friday before the meeting after the Neue Luzerner Zeitung published a report quoting SNB chairman Meyer. He was quoted by the Swiss paper as saying the SNB would have to tighten rates once the economy took off.
Conf futures CONFc1 up six at 118.49.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 flat at 111.05
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 down one at 98.03.
